headlines.title: Building an Advanced Agentic Harness
headlines.summary: A working writeup of the control plane around a coding agent: tools, memory, retries, and the loop that actually lands code. Blueprint material if you are assembling your own harness.

headlines.title: HUD, a minimal terminal UI for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode
headlines.summary: A compact heads-up display that instruments a coding agent while it works. Shipped this day. Power-user overlay the big CLIs do not bother to build.

headlines.title: Harness engineering for self-improvement
headlines.summary: Weng's essay on the scaffolding around self-improving agents. The claim is that the harness, not the next model bump, is where competence compounds.

perfected.label: Perfected
perfected.algorithm: GitHub-first power-user stack. Obscure, recently shipped harnesses a working engineer would actually clone.
perfected.title: Control planes for agents you already run
perfected.blurb: Five GitHub-native harnesses power users actually wire around their coding agents: long-horizon control, sandboxed workers, context compression, and a Go binary that repairs its own code.

tools.title: LoopX
tools.summary: A long-horizon control plane that keeps coding agents on durable, governed work instead of one-shot chats.
tools.usecase: Use it to keep an overnight refactor alive across tool crashes, with a human gate on the risky steps.

tools.title: Omnigent
tools.summary: Open-source meta-harness: one orchestrator that fans work across several coding agents. Born June 2026.
tools.usecase: Use it to run three different coding agents on the same ticket and merge the first one that lands a green test.

tools.title: Warren
tools.summary: Treats coding agents as infrastructure, not terminal sessions. Isolation, lifetimes, scheduling.
tools.usecase: Use it to fire 20 isolated agent jobs against a monorepo without them trampling each other's working trees.

tools.title: context-mode
tools.summary: Context-window surgery for coding agents. Sandboxes tool output so the model sees signal instead of a 40k-token log.
tools.usecase: Use it when your agent keeps blowing the window on build logs and you need the loop to survive a real compile.

tools.title: Agenvoy
tools.summary: Self-hosted agent harness in a single Go binary. Writes, sandbox-tests, and repairs its own code.
tools.usecase: Use it as a local coding worker you can scp onto a box and run unattended against a failing test suite.

velocity.label: Algorithm A: GitHub velocity
velocity.algorithm: Created in 2026, still pushing, 100-15k stars. Recency of push ranks first.
velocity.title: What GitHub started shipping this year
velocity.blurb: Five agent runtimes and ADEs created in 2026 and still moving. Ranked by recency and whether you can run them tonight, not by brand.

tools.title: Orca
tools.summary: An ADE for a fleet of parallel agents. Run any coding agent against your repo in parallel panes.
tools.usecase: Use it to fan the same failing test across four agents and keep only the patch that compiles.

tools.title: Herdr
tools.summary: The runtime your coding agents live on. Persist, resume, share a machine.
tools.usecase: Use it when you want agents to survive a laptop sleep and pick up the same checkout, secrets, and tools.

tools.title: cmux
tools.summary: Open-source Ghostty-based macOS terminal with vertical tabs and notifications for AI coding agents.
tools.usecase: Use it as the terminal surface when you are running a swarm of CLIs and need to see which one just finished.

tools.title: oh-my-pi
tools.summary: A coding agent with the IDE wired in. Created New Year's Eve 2025, still being pushed daily.
tools.usecase: Use it when you want the agent and the editor to share one process instead of a plugin talking to a CLI.

tools.title: oh-my-claudecode
tools.summary: Teams-first multi-agent orchestration for Claude Code. Not Claude Code itself: the swarm layer people bolt on.
tools.usecase: Use it to run a team of Claude Code workers on one repo with a shared plan file.

research.label: Algorithm B: Research origin
research.algorithm: Started as a paper, lab, or benchmark, now clone-and-run.
research.title: Lab software you can actually run
research.blurb: Five repos that left the paper and became a loop: SWE-agent lineage, HKU DeepCode, OSWorld computer-use, E2B desktop, LastMile MCP.

tools.title: mini-SWE-agent
tools.summary: The 100-line agent from the Princeton SWE-agent line. Research origin, radical simplicity.
tools.usecase: Use it to throw a GitHub issue at a 100-line loop you can actually read, fork, and instrument.

tools.title: DeepCode
tools.summary: Open agentic coding from HKU: harness, loop engineering, multi-agent orchestration.
tools.usecase: Use it when you want a research harness with a real coding loop, not a chatbot with extra steps.

tools.title: open-computer-use
tools.summary: Computer-use agents on open models plus an E2B desktop sandbox.
tools.usecase: Use it to let an open model click through a desktop app inside a throwaway VM.

tools.title: mcp-agent
tools.summary: Effective agents with Model Context Protocol and small workflow patterns.
tools.usecase: Use it to compose MCP servers into a durable agent without standing up a full IDE plugin.

tools.title: OSWorld 2.0
tools.summary: Long-horizon computer-use benchmark. The eval serious desktop-agent repos cite.
tools.usecase: Use it to grade your own computer-use agent on real desktop tasks before you trust it on a laptop.

infra.label: Algorithm C: Infra under the agent
infra.algorithm: No coding CLI. Runtimes, memory, context, computer-use, policy.
infra.title: The layer under the coding agent
infra.blurb: You already have a coding agent. These five make it survive: memory, context compression, desktop drivers, a policy runtime, and artifact verification.

tools.title: Mnemon
tools.summary: LLM-supervised persistent memory: graph recall, cross-session knowledge.
tools.usecase: Use it to give a coding agent a graph of the last two weeks of decisions so it stops re-deriving your architecture.

tools.title: context-mode
tools.summary: Sandboxes tool output so coding agents stop drowning in logs.
tools.usecase: Use it when compile output is killing the context window mid-loop.

tools.title: CUA
tools.summary: Open-source computer-use 2.0: drivers, cross-OS fleets, benchmarks.
tools.usecase: Use it to give a coding agent a real desktop when the job is a GUI installer, not an API.

tools.title: Ironcurtain
tools.summary: Secure runtime for autonomous agents. Policy from plain-English constitutions.
tools.usecase: Use it when you will not give a coding agent root and still want it to act.

tools.title: oh-my-agent
tools.summary: Checks the work by artifacts, not vibes. Stop-hooks verify diffs and tests.
tools.usecase: Use it to stop a coding agent from declaring done when the test file was never written.

systems.label: Algorithm D: Systems-language harnesses
systems.algorithm: Go, Rust, Zig, C++. Small star counts. No Electron.
systems.title: Harnesses that are not another Node wrapper
systems.blurb: Go, Zig, and Rust control planes. Single binaries you can scp. Built by people tired of Electron agent UIs.

tools.title: Agenvoy
tools.summary: Self-hosted harness in one Go binary. Writes, sandbox-tests, repairs its own code.
tools.usecase: Use it as an unattended local worker against a failing test suite.

tools.title: graff
tools.summary: Fast agentic coding harness in Zig: multi-provider, MCP, workflows.
tools.usecase: Use it when you want a coding loop with systems-language latency, not a Node daemon.

tools.title: Whip
tools.summary: Fast coding-agent harness in Go. Tool-use loop, bubbletea TUI, provider-routable models. Created August 2026.
tools.usecase: Use it as a Go TUI coding agent when you want to swap models without swapping the loop.

tools.title: Ghostex
tools.summary: Rust and GPUI native agent CLI manager for macOS. Ghostty terminals plus Codex-app UX, without Electron.
tools.usecase: Use it to manage a stack of native agent CLIs in Ghostty instead of a webview IDE.

tools.title: Containarium
tools.summary: Open-source agent runtime with SSH-native isolation, eBPF egress policy, Kubernetes and LXC backends.
tools.usecase: Use it to run untrusted coding agents with real network policy instead of hope.
